headline: SRA: El Niño, pests, high costs may cut sugar output further
summary: The Sugar Regulatory Administration said weak production, rising farm costs, El Nino and pest infestation may reduce sugar output further. It did not say whether output could fall below its 1.662 million metric ton projection for 2026-2027.
why: Sugar is an agricultural commodity, and domestic output shortfalls affect supply, prices and imports in the Philippines, which relies on both local production and imports.
